draft.title: The United Nations
card: The United Nations (UN) was founded in 1945, just after the Second World War. Its main aim was to keep international peace and prevent another world war.

Member states meet in the General Assembly, where each has one vote. The Security Council deals with threats to peace. The United States, the Soviet Union, Britain, France and China held permanent seats.
The UN also took on other work. In 1948 it adopted the Universal Declaration of Human Rights, a statement of rights for all people.
It also worked on economic and social problems, such as poverty and health, and helped refugees, who are people forced to flee their homes.
draft.remember: The UN began to keep peace and also worked on rights, social problems and refugees.

a.q: What was the main reason the United Nations was founded in 1945?
opts: To keep international peace after the war
To manage trade between member countries
To rule over the countries that joined
To help only refugees return home
a.why: The UN was set up to stop another world war. It later took on other work, such as refugees, but that was not its main founding aim. It was not a government over its members.
a.clue: Think about what the world had just been through.

b.q: In 1948 the UN adopted a statement of rights that should apply to all people. What was it?
opts: The Universal Declaration of Human Rights
The Security Council charter of rights
The General Assembly peace treaty
The Declaration of Refugee Relief
b.why: The Universal Declaration of Human Rights was adopted in 1948 and shows the UN's work beyond peacekeeping. The other titles are invented and do not name that statement.
b.clue: The name says what it covers: rights for humans.

a.best: To keep international peace after the war

b.best: The Universal Declaration of Human Rights

problems.detail: The clue ('The name says what it covers: rights for humans') points straight at the only option containing 'Human Rights'. Combined with the question's 'apply to all people' echoing 'Universal', a student can pick the answer without knowing it.

b.q: A student claims the UN's only job was to stop wars between states. Which UN action best shows the student is wrong?
opts: Giving aid to people forced to flee their homes
A Security Council debate on a threat to peace
A General Assembly vote to end a border war
Permanent members meeting to stop an invasion
b.why: Helping refugees is UN work beyond keeping peace, so it shows the student's claim is wrong. The other three are the Security Council or General Assembly acting against wars, which fits the claim rather than disproving it.
b.clue: Which action is not about stopping a war?

a.best: To keep international peace after the war

b.best: Giving aid to people forced to flee their homes
